$comment: Release notes for commits merged before they could declare their own with 'Release-note:' trailers. Read by build/scripts/SetReleaseNotesArgument.ps1. Each key is a full commit id; 'subject' is the commit's subject, checked to catch a wrong id; 'notes' replaces every note the commit would otherwise produce, and an empty list leaves it out. Categories: added, new, fixed, changed, deprecated, removed, breaking, none.

5b46a0f120d00b8def7695bda204c547c6767085.subject: Build AnyCPU only: remove the x86 and x64 build platforms (#127) (#203)

2fc3453d27d0220231e229cec373a8a36a4822d3.subject: Add the File.iCal docs, README row and benchmarks (#190) (#214)

9ecf663ca0b84be1f75d677383834ffe68d6a56a.subject: Keep the last observance on a tied onset in GetUtcOffset (#262) (#279)

notes.text: When two observances of a calendar's VTIMEZONE begin at the same instant, GetUtcOffset now uses the last of them, as GetTransitions does, so ToUtc and ToLocal agree with the transitions

db8b5808bba187a1a01c679b0ef35f82c96bd71e.subject: Cache VTIMEZONE observance onsets by year (#263, #280) (#281)

notes.text: A VTIMEZONE RDATE onset no longer takes effect up to a second early for an instant with a fraction of a second
Resolving times through a calendar's own VTIMEZONE, the default resolver, is faster and allocates less, because observance onsets are now expanded once per year and reused

88beb77e6c12af71068a508252cabfdcf665f823.subject: Replace the alarm TRIGGER in place from either setter (#264, #282) (#283)

notes.text: Setting IcalAlarm.TriggerDateTime, or TriggerDuration on an alarm with an absolute trigger, now keeps the TRIGGER's other parameters and its position instead of dropping them and moving it to the end

56c0aeeb803c8e4ee8ceed4d1689405a5b675c91.subject: IcalTimeZoneResolver.Calendar rules give the right offset before a VTIMEZONE's first onset (#294)

notes.text: IcalTimeZoneResolver.Calendar rules give the right offset before a VTIMEZONE's first onset

319bcf011b3ae8b27eec7bc560c72bcd08359eb8.subject: Language tags that repeat a variant subtag or extension singleton are rejected (#318)

notes.text: A language tag that repeats a variant subtag or an extension singleton, ignoring case, is rejected as RFC 5646 requires, by `Create`, `TryCreate`, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` and the builder's `UsingVariantSubtags` and `UsingExtensionSubtags`

8c69c57005bf9342550d31c56bb1c694e10acdd7.subject: Default rules follow the RFC 5646 primary language subtag grammar (#320)

notes.text: Without a subtag registry, primary language subtags follow RFC 5646: one of five to eight characters must be letters only, so `12345` is rejected, and an extended language subtag must follow one of two or three letters, so `abcde-yue` is rejected
Without a subtag registry, four-letter primary language subtags, which RFC 5646 reserves for future use, are accepted as well-formed

fb24de6b9156b8db2f12f081b236c882a4c6ca5e.subject: Builder takes a UN M49 area through UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49Area) (#326)

notes.text: `Bcp47LanguageTagBuilder.UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49Area)` sets a UN M.49 area such as `UnM49Area._419` (Latin America and the Caribbean) as the region, and throws `ArgumentException` for a country

The builder's `UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49AreaByAlpha2CountryCode)` and `UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49AreaByAlpha3CountryCode)` overloads are obsolete, because they reject every member of those enums, and will be removed in v2.0; use `UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49Area)` or `UsingRegionSubtag(Iso3166Part1Alpha2Country)`

983790fa282c26c630e5065be0b2132a438952bd.subject: Language tag and subtag matching no longer depends on the current culture or accepts non-ASCII letters (#335)

notes.text: Language tag and subtag validation no longer depends on the current culture or accepts non-ASCII letters, so `IT` is accepted under the Turkish culture and the Kelvin sign (U+212A) is not accepted in place of `K`

eae2dbcc625c731b0291f3d03edd478a8a7d442d.subject: Default rules validate language tags with a parser instead of regular expressions (#322)

notes.text: Validation by the default BCP 47 rules uses a parser instead of regular expressions: the first Create is about 20 times faster, later calls 30 to 300 times faster, and validation no longer allocates
The netstandard2.0 build depends on System.Memory

fa92dfa9c0423fc27e102b6a675c20dfb30cbad5.subject: Language tags are checked against a Subtag Registry with a parser instead of regular expressions (#338)

notes.text: Checking a language tag against a Subtag Registry uses a parser instead of regular expressions: Create is about 10,000 times faster, the first call in a process takes milliseconds instead of more than a second, and checking no longer allocates
Creating language tags against the same Subtag Registry from several threads at once no longer throws or corrupts a shared cache
A Subtag Registry with no grandfathered records, or no records of some subtag type, no longer accepts the empty string or a tag with an empty subtag such as "en-"

7e8c6ce9762adc90656f31fb2d08f6ed44547947.subject: Default rules accept the grandfathered language tags as whole tags (#319)

notes.text: Without a subtag registry, the irregular grandfathered tags, such as `i-klingon` and `en-GB-oed`, are accepted as RFC 5646 requires

Without a subtag registry, regular grandfathered tags such as `art-lojban` are treated as whole tags, as they are with one: `PrimaryLanguageSubtag` is empty and the other subtag properties are `null` or empty

736c5c2458bf8e57f6f365f557b0e415c77b8835.subject: Default rules reject the unregistered region subtag 830 (#321)

notes.text: Without a subtag registry, the region subtag `830` (Channel Islands), which isn't in the IANA Language Subtag Registry, is rejected as RFC 5646 requires

efc410ebc3bb5a0dc7928b3b587ad52887c97267.subject: TryCreate(tag, registry, timeout, out) accepts tags that are valid only in the Subtag Registry (#333)

notes.text: `TryCreate(string, SubtagRegistry, TimeSpan, out Bcp47LanguageTag)` accepts tags that are valid only in the Subtag Registry, as the other registry overloads do

cf1066d2a70498b186c78e9b8f78893b688dc015.subject: Loading a Subtag Registry is about 2.3 times faster and allocates 73% less (#345)

notes.text: Loading a Subtag Registry is about 2.3 times faster and allocates 73% less

Loading a Subtag Registry unfolds a folded Description or Comments value with one space, skips an empty record or one with no File-Date, Subtag or Tag field instead of stopping there, and reads a field it doesn't know as a field of its own instead of appending it to the field before

496343f8601596f462338194deb06a6999fd014d.subject: Bcp47LanguageTag validates and parses spans of characters, and implements ISpanParsable and ISpanFormattable (#347)

notes.text: On netstandard2.0 and .NET 8 and later, `Bcp47LanguageTag.TryCreate`, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` and the `Check*` methods accept a `ReadOnlySpan<char>`; only `TryCreate` allocates, and only to copy a valid tag to a string. `AsSpan()` returns the tag without copying it
`Bcp47LanguageTag` implements `IParsable<T>` and `ISpanParsable<T>` on .NET 7 and later, and `ISpanFormattable` on .NET 6 and later

The new span overloads make a literal `null` or `default` argument to `TryCreate`, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` or a `Check*` method ambiguous on C# 7.3; cast it to `string`. On C# 10 and later, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` and the `Check*` methods can no longer be assigned to `var`; give the variable a delegate type such as `Func<string, bool>`. `Type.GetMethod(name)` throws `AmbiguousMatchException` for them; pass the parameter types. Compiled code is unaffected

11c7e3783e507ee0dc0da8bac146e3b092dcb0d9.subject: Decode and encode RFC 2231 parameter continuations, character sets and languages in MimeMediaType (#464)

notes.text: `MimeMediaType` decodes RFC 2231 parameter sections and extended values (character set and language), and rejects anything RFC 2231 doesn't allow unless the caller opts in with a `MimeMediaTypeParseOptions` member: `AllowMissingSections`, `AllowDuplicateSections` and `AllowLeadingZeroSectionNumbers` (together, `AllowNonstandardSections`), `AllowQuotedExtendedValues` and `AllowLowercaseHexDigits` (together, `AllowNonstandardExtendedValues`), `AllowUnknownCharsets` and `AllowInvalidOctets`
`MimeParameter` takes values that aren't US-ASCII and an optional RFC 1766 language, writes them as RFC 2231 extended values, and splits long parameters into sections with `FormatSections`
